bank-0001.purpose: This goal builds the student's ability to share and seek information, using their preferred communication method. That lets the student learn, contribute ideas, and be understood beyond basic wants and needs.
activityIdeas: During a familiar daily routine, model the language through the student's preferred communication method for a comment or question about what is happening, pause and honor wait time, and accept any contribution in the modality the goal allows, no correct answer required.

During another everyday routine, model the language through the student's preferred communication method for sharing a short piece of information or asking about a familiar topic, pause and honor wait time without filling the silence, and build on whatever the student shares, including a refusal to answer.

bank-0002.purpose: This goal builds the student's ability to share and seek information with adults, using their preferred communication method. That lets the student learn, contribute ideas, and be understood beyond basic wants and needs.
activityIdeas: During a routine with an adult, model the language through the student's preferred communication method for a comment or question about what is happening, pause and honor wait time, and accept any contribution in the modality the goal allows, no correct answer required.

During another everyday interaction with an adult, model the language through the student's preferred communication method for sharing a short piece of information or asking about a familiar topic, pause and honor wait time without filling the silence, and build on whatever the student shares, including a refusal to answer.

bank-0003.purpose: This goal builds skills in clarification & Repair with adults, using whatever way of communicating the student uses. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During a routine with an adult, set up a planned misunderstanding, an unclear direction, or the wrong item named, then model noticing the breakdown and one way to repair it, such as restating, adding detail, or showing; pause and honor wait time, and accept any repair attempt in the modality the goal allows.

During another everyday interaction with an adult, let a genuine mix-up happen, or stage another small one; model the language using the student's preferred way of communicating for a repair move, pause and honor wait time without solving it for the student, and build on whatever the student does, including signaling someone else for help.

bank-0004.purpose: This goal builds skills in audience & Register with a communication partner, using their preferred communication method. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During a familiar daily routine with a communication partner, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to notice when an unfamiliar listener needs more background and will supply relevant background information; model the language through the student's preferred communication method once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During another everyday routine with a communication partner, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to notice when an unfamiliar listener needs more background and will supply relevant background information; model the language through the student's preferred communication method without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0005.purpose: This goal builds the student's ability to request and obtain what they need or want and share and seek information with adults, using their preferred communication method. Together, those moves support agency, participation, and being understood across everyday routines.
activityIdeas: During a routine with an adult, set up a natural need for a wanted item or for help; model the language through the student's preferred communication method for a request, pause and honor wait time, and respond to any request attempt in the modality the goal allows.

During another everyday interaction with an adult, model the language through the student's preferred communication method for sharing a short piece of information or asking about a familiar topic, pause and honor wait time without filling the silence, and build on whatever the student shares, including a refusal to answer.

bank-0006.purpose: This goal builds skills in clarification & Repair, using their preferred communication method. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.

During another everyday routine, let a genuine mix-up happen, or stage another small one; model the language through the student's preferred communication method for a repair move, pause and honor wait time without solving it for the student, and build on whatever the student does, including signaling someone else for help.

bank-0007.purpose: This goal builds the student's ability to refuse or protest when something is not wanted with adults, using their preferred communication method. That protects choice, safety, and boundaries, and refusal itself is valid communication the student can use in everyday life.
activityIdeas: During a routine with an adult, offer a real choice where saying no is an option; model the language through the student's preferred communication method for a refusal, pause and honor wait time, and honor any refusal or protest as valid communication.

During another everyday interaction with an adult, pause before a non-preferred step; model the language through the student's preferred communication method for “no” or “stop”, pause and honor wait time without repeating the prompt, and accept the response in any modality the goal allows, no correct response required.

bank-0008.purpose: This goal builds skills in audience & Register with a communication partner, using their preferred communication method. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During a familiar daily routine with a communication partner, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to describe how the amount of information, word choice, or communication style may shift depending on the listener; model the language through the student's preferred communication method once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During another everyday routine with a communication partner, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to describe how the amount of information, word choice, or communication style may shift depending on the listener; model the language through the student's preferred communication method without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0009.purpose: This goal builds skills in conversation: Turns & Topic with peers, using multimodal communication. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During shared time with peers, hold a short back-and-forth on a familiar topic or in a shared activity; model finishing your own turn and pausing for the student's turn, pause and honor wait time, and accept a turn taken in any modality the goal allows, a turn does not have to be spoken.

During another peer activity, take turns adding one piece at a time, a turn in a game, a line in a shared story, a step in a routine; model the language using multimodal communication for waiting and then responding, pause and honor wait time without filling the student's turn, and follow the student's timing.

activityIdeas: During shared time with peers, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to express agreement or disagreement with a peer opinion using a clear phrase or symbol selection; model the language using the student's preferred way of communicating once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During a group activity with a peer, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to express agreement or disagreement with a peer opinion using a clear phrase or symbol selection; model the language using the student's preferred way of communicating without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0327.purpose: This goal builds skills in expressive Language with peers or a teacher or staff member during classroom routines, using their AAC system or spoken words. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During class time, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to name/label objects, pictures, school staff, peers, and/or classroom activities (verbally or via AAC) with ___% verbal, physical; model the language using their AAC system or spoken words once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During shared time with peers, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to name/label objects, pictures, school staff, peers, and/or classroom activities (verbally or via AAC) with ___% verbal, physical; model the language using their AAC system or spoken words without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

During another classroom routine, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to perform sentence/phrase completion tasks related to classroom routines and safety (verbally or via AAC) with ___% visual,; model the language using their AAC system or spoken words without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0329.purpose: This goal builds skills in expressive Language during classroom routines, using their preferred communication method. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During class time, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to formulate sentences/multi-symbol messages with given core/fringe words related to personal needs, classroom tasks, and safety; model the language through the student's preferred communication method once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During another classroom routine, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to formulate sentences/multi-symbol messages with given core/fringe words related to personal needs, classroom tasks, and safety; model the language through the student's preferred communication method without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0330.purpose: This goal builds skills in conversation: Turns & Topic with peers or a communication partner, using multimodal communication. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During shared time with peers, hold a short back-and-forth on a familiar topic or in a shared activity; model finishing your own turn and pausing for the student's turn, pause and honor wait time, and accept a turn taken in any modality the goal allows, a turn does not have to be spoken.

During another peer activity, take turns adding one piece at a time, a turn in a game, a line in a shared story, a step in a routine; model the language using multimodal communication for waiting and then responding, pause and honor wait time without filling the student's turn, and follow the student's timing.

bank-0331.purpose: This goal builds skills in expressive Language during classroom routines, using their AAC system or spoken words. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During class time, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to use short phrases / 2-4 word combinations (verbally or via AAC) to communicate experiences, preferences, and classroom ideas with; model the language using their AAC system or spoken words once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During another classroom routine, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to use short phrases / 2-4 word combinations (verbally or via AAC) to communicate experiences, preferences, and classroom ideas with; model the language using their AAC system or spoken words without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0332.purpose: This goal builds skills in conversation: Turns & Topic with a teacher or staff member during group activities, using whatever way of communicating the student uses. That matters because it supports participation, learning, and being understood in everyday routines, on the student's own terms.
activityIdeas: During a group activity with a teacher or staff member, set up the situation this goal names, with a natural moment for the student to make 10 appropriate communicative utterances/selections during a 15-minute group activity in response to props and minimal; model the language using the student's preferred way of communicating once, pause and honor wait time, and accept any attempt in the modality the goal allows, no correct response required and no hand-over-hand prompting.

During another group activity with a teacher or staff member, offer the same kind of moment again, watching for a chance for the student to make 10 appropriate communicative utterances/selections during a 15-minute group activity in response to props and minimal; model the language using the student's preferred way of communicating without demanding imitation, pause and honor wait time, and note what the student does, including choosing not to respond.

bank-0333.purpose: This goal builds the student's ability to notice and interpret other people's communication with peers or a teacher or staff member, and to respond in their own way. That matters because reading the cues and messages others send helps the student follow what is happening and choose how to respond, this goal is about taking communication in, not producing a set response.

During another peer activity, offer another natural example; model noticing the cue before naming what it might mean, pause and honor wait time without filling the silence, and build on whatever the student indicates, including choosing not to respond.
